observations: 2026-08-11: Miami's first depth chart of the preseason — explicitly unofficial — lists the starting WRs as Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington, with Tutu Atwell, Terrace Marshall Jr., and Theo Wease Jr. behind them; the preseason opener is Friday 08-15 vs. Washington (Local10, 08-11). HC Jeff Hafley (team-official, via PFT 08-12): 'It's been consistency over time... he's probably been one of our most consistent guys, and he's showed up every day. So that's where he deserves to be at this point.'

Draft context (2026-04-25): Miami selected Douglas at No. 75 overall (Round 3); NFL.com's Lance Zierlein had projected him as a fifth- or sixth-round pick — a materially earlier selection than that public expectation (Palm Beach Post via Yahoo, 04-25). Dolphins director of college scouting Matt Winston: 'Caleb brings some size to the room, a good athlete can run the full route tree.'

Target-competition context: Jaylen Waddle was traded to Denver (reported 2026-03-18, finalized at the draft) and Tyreek Hill was released by the new regime and remains a free agent — the Miami WR room's incumbent target hierarchy was structurally cleared before camp.

2026-08-12 joint practice at Washington: Douglas recorded multiple catches from Malik Willis over the middle and drew a defensive penalty (Palm Beach Post/Joe Schad via Yahoo, 08-12). Douglas: 'You've got to keep working, man. It's not in stone yet.'

~2026-08-10: Dolphins GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, on The Joe Rose Show (104.3 WQAM), discussed Douglas after nine camp practices: 'Caleb has a LOT of natural gifts... it's the body type. He's tall, he's long, he can run... he can bend. He can get in and out of breaks. Got extremely quick feet and, like all of them, he's honing his craft... Some of the hard lessons he's learned early on, he's starting to reap the benefits of that.' (A to Z Sports, 08-10). Recorded as team-evaluator characterization, not on-field performance evidence.
inferences: Directional mechanism (pre-baseline, preserved as inference): role/access opportunity is unusually open — the starter listing plus the Waddle/Hill departures point to immediate route/snap access; none of this quantifies a target share.
Any player-quality interpretation (draft-capital read, GM characterization, camp flashes) is inference and is kept separate from the access evidence above.
The depth-chart first listing is not converted into a WR1 target-share claim; positive coach/GM speak is not converted into production.
